vars.prTitle: Treat non-positive RequiredActionProvider max auth age as unset
vars.prBody: Custom required actions that read their max auth age from an empty/unset config ended up returning 0, which forces a re-authentication on every application-initiated action. Clarify the RequiredActionProvider#getMaxAuthAge contract (seconds; <= 0 means not defined by the action) and fall back to the default KC_ACTION_MAX_AGE in OIDCLoginProtocol.
vars.goldenComments: [{"comment": "The RequiredActionProvider#getMaxAuthAge contract previously said '0 means that re-authentication is always requested', and OIDCLoginProtocol.isReAuthRequiredForKcAction now maps any value <= 0 to Constants.KC_ACTION_MAX_AGE (300s). Built-in implementations rely on 0 meaning 'always re-authenticate': DeleteAccount.getMaxAuthAge() returns 0 so that kc_action=delete_account always requires a fresh login; after this change a user who logged in within the last 5 minutes (or an attacker with a briefly unattended session) can delete the account without re-authenticating. UpdatePassword.getMaxAuthAge() also returns a configured maxAuthAge of 0 from the password policy / action config as 'always', which is now silently turned into 300s. This is a security regression in the AIA re-auth check.", "severity": "High"}]
